chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from a man he mentioned, from Suleiman ibn Khalid, who said:

Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said to me: 'What did you do to my uncle Zayd?' I said, 'They were guarding him, so when the people dispersed, we took his body and buried him in a cliff on the shore of the Euphrates. When it was morning, the horsemen came looking for him, so they found him and burnt him.'
He said: 'So why did you not tie iron to him and throw him in the Euphrates? Greetings of Allah be upon him, and Curse of Allah be upon his killers.'
Greetings of Allah be upon him, and Curse of Allah be upon his killers.

key_terms.أَوْقَرْتُمُوهُ: you weighted him / made him heavy

ai.seo_question: How did Imam al-Sadiq (AS) advise handling the burial of his uncle Zayd to prevent enemies from finding and burning his body?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) critiques the hasty burial of his uncle Zayd in a shallow cliff on the Euphrates, noting that the ease of discovery led to his body being burnt by pursuers. He advises that weighting the body with iron and submerging it in the river would have ensured complete concealment, reflecting the Shia emphasis on preserving the dignity of the Ahl al-Bayt against public desecration. This incident highlights the practical wisdom of the Imams in managing the physical security of their family members during periods of political persecution.
